summary.oneLiner: Diversified pharmaceutical formulations company with branded-generic and CDMO capabilities across injectables, tablets, capsules, liquid orals and ointments.
summary.business: Sai Parenteral is a diversified pharma formulations company operating in (i) Branded Generic Formulations sold under its own brands to government agencies, pharma companies, hospitals and super-stockists, and (ii) CDMO products & services (product development, validation, stability studies, dossiers, regulatory filings, commercial manufacturing) for domestic and international (Regulated and Semi-Regulated) markets. It owns 5 manufacturing facilities in India and acquired a 74.60% stake in Noumed Pharmaceuticals (Australia/NZ) in November 2025.

currentContext.business: Sai Parenteral is a diversified pharma formulations company operating in (i) Branded Generic Formulations sold under its own brands to government agencies, pharma companies, hospitals and super-stockists, and (ii) CDMO products & services (product development, validation, stability studies, dossiers, regulatory filings, commercial manufacturing) for domestic and international (Regulated and Semi-Regulated) markets. currentContext.expansion: Capacity expansion and upgradation of Units I-IV (targeting EU-GMP/PIC/S accreditations) plus a new R&D centre; Noumed's Australian factory under development, expected complete Q4 CY2026 (AUD 20 million Australian government grant disbursed).

one-line thesis: Sai Parenterals is a vertically integrated Indian pharmaceutical player scaling its global CDMO platform through strategic acquisitions in Australia and New Zealand, backed by regulatory-approved manufacturing and a growing dossier pipeline. The company is leveraging its expanded capacity and R&D center to capture high-margin export opportunities in regulated markets with strong visibility from long-term contracts.
guidance / outlook: Strong export-led growth outlook for FY27 and beyond, driven by CDMO contracts, new facility commissioning in Adelaide (Q4FY27), and R&D pipeline acceleration. Focus on expanding branded generics in international markets and enhancing margins through higher-value complex products.
order book & pipeline: Exclusive long-term CDMO supply agreements with Australian pharmacy chains; multiple regulated-market product registrations under development; 67 dossiers in pipeline
segment / subsidiary detail: CDMO revenue surged 250% YoY in FY26; 456 TGA-Australia approvals; 143 approvals in other markets; 302 complex products across injectables, tablets, capsules, orals, sprays; Noumed contributes Rx and OTC access in Australia/NZ; 74.6% stake in Noumed consolidated from Nov 2025
growth verticals / optionality: Expansion into Asia, Middle East, Latin America via leveraged regulatory dossiers; potential for new product launches from SP Analytics R&D center; upside from two-shift operations at existing facilities; possible further acquisitions in regulated markets
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin improved from 20% (FY25) to 24% (Q4FY26); PAT margin improved from 10% to 12% (Q4FY26); cost efficiencies from scale, vertical integration, and CDMO mix shift; capex-driven capacity expansion expected to improve unit economics over time
capex / expansion: Total capex of ₹111 crore from IPO proceeds allocated to manufacturing upgrades (Units I, II, III, IV); ₹18 crore for SP Analytics R&D center; AUD 53 million (₹2,800+ crore) for Adelaide facility (AUD 20 million grant received); total capex FY26-27 exceeds ₹3,000 crore
capital allocation: IPO proceeds allocated: ₹111cr (capex), ₹18cr (R&D), ₹36cr (Noumed debt repayment), ₹33cr (working capital), ₹28cr (corporate/general); focus on debt reduction, capacity expansion, and R&D; no dividend policy disclosed
risks & watch-items: Regulatory delays in EU-GMP upgrades; execution risk in Adelaide facility commissioning (Q4FY27); currency volatility in AUD/NZD; customer concentration in Australian pharmacy chains; competition from global CDMOs; reliance on expiring patents for R&D pipeline; integration risks from recent acquisitions
non-obvious takeaways: Noumed’s Australian CDMO business is underpinned by exclusive supply agreements with pharmacy chains — a rare, sticky revenue model in generics; the AUD 20M government grant for Adelaide facility is non-dilutive capital, reducing financial risk; SP Analytics’ 67-dossier pipeline is targeted at patent cliffs within 3 years, creating a high-probability launch runway

themes.title: Pharma CDMO / CRDMO & API import-substitution
themes.need: Global biopharma's China+1 sourcing plus a peptide/biologics modality boom drive India's CDMO/CRDMO build-out and API import-substitution. ANTHEM/COHANCE/NEULANDLAB/SYNGENE-tier on CRDMO (peptides/ADCs/oligos); DIVISLAB/LAURUSLABS on peptide CDMO; AKUMS/INNOVACAP/RUBICON on formulation CDMO; AARTIPHARM/SUPRIYA/AARTIDRUGS/SOLARA on APIs; SIGACHI/NATCAPSUQ/VIDHIING on excipients.
themes.driver: Customer regulatory filings unlocking dedicated capacity; new CRDMO molecule wins; API price/volume recovery.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Diversified pharmaceutical formulations company with branded-generic and CDMO capabilities across injectables, tablets, capsules, liquid orals and ointments.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Two verticals on one platform: CDMO Products & Services at 63% of FY26 net revenue (deck-stated 355.6% CAGR over FY23-FY26) and Branded Generic Formulations at 37% (deck-stated 15.6% CAGR over FY23-FY26). The deck states no CDMO work is undertaken domestically — the entire contract book serves export markets.
- Export revenue rose from 3% of Revenue from Operations in FY23 to 63% in FY26 (16.3% in FY25); private-sector share of revenue rose from 39% in FY23 to 81% in FY26 "as tender exposure recedes".
- The Noumed platform: 74.64% of Noumed Pharmaceuticals (Australia and New Zealand) acquired for AUD 22 million (including a primary infusion of AUD 4.00 million), completed 12th Nov 2025, bringing 451+ TGA dossiers, pharmacy-chain relationships and last-mile commercialisation. Deck claims Noumed is "the only organisation in Australia offering the full turnkey solution to multinational pharmaceutical companies".
- Australian pharmacy structure is the stated moat: chains own the consumer brand but hold no registrations and do no manufacturing; Noumed holds the marketing authorisation, the inventory and the logistics. 2,900 of Australia's 5,500 pharmacies are covered by the Wesfarmers Health, EBOS and Sandoz (Chemist Warehouse) networks.
- Contracted international revenue named in the deck: AUD 202 mn over a 7.5-year exclusive OTC supply agreement in Australia through Noumed, effective 1 July 2026, at approximately AUD 27 mn per annum (plus a 3-year option); and USD 11 mn on a 4-year exclusive anti-tuberculosis contract in the Philippines (from June 2026).

cost_leadership.body: Manufacturing-led; began exports in FY2023 after acquiring accredited Hyderabad units (Unit III, IV); backward via in-house FR&D and dossier development; forward via Noumed distribution in Australia/NZ.

guidance.body: Strong export-led growth outlook for FY27 and beyond, driven by CDMO contracts, new facility commissioning in Adelaide (Q4FY27), and R&D pipeline acceleration. Focus on expanding branded generics in international markets and enhancing margins through higher-value complex products.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Expansion into Asia, Middle East, Latin America via leveraged regulatory dossiers; potential for new product launches from SP Analytics R&D center; upside from two-shift operations at existing facilities; possible further acquisitions in regulated markets

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Shift in mix from injectables toward tablets and CDMO
- Export ramp since FY2023 after acquiring accredited Hyderabad units
- Working-capital intensity of government/institutional sales

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: EBITDA margin improved from 20% (FY25) to 24% (Q4FY26); PAT margin improved from 10% to 12% (Q4FY26); cost efficiencies from scale, vertical integration, and CDMO mix shift; capex-driven capacity expansion expected to improve unit economics over time

capital_allocation.body: IPO proceeds allocated: ₹111cr (capex), ₹18cr (R&D), ₹36cr (Noumed debt repayment), ₹33cr (working capital), ₹28cr (corporate/general); focus on debt reduction, capacity expansion, and R&D; no dividend policy disclosed

capex_expansion.title: Expansion (RHP)
capex_expansion.body: Capacity expansion and upgradation of Units I-IV (targeting EU-GMP/PIC/S accreditations) plus a new R&D centre; Noumed's Australian factory under development, expected complete Q4 CY2026 (AUD 20 million Australian government grant disbursed).

moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body:
- Diversified formulations portfolio across therapeutic areas and dosage forms incl. sterile injectables
- Internationally accredited facilities (TGA-Australia, WHO-GMP, PIC/S) enabling Regulated-market exports
- Growing CDMO vertical (5.5% of revenue FY23 to 19.7% FY25)
- Inorganic expansion (Revat Labs, Noumed Australia/NZ)

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Regulatory delays in EU-GMP upgrades; execution risk in Adelaide facility commissioning (Q4FY27); currency volatility in AUD/NZD; customer concentration in Australian pharmacy chains; competition from global CDMOs; reliance on expiring patents for R&D pipeline; integration risks from recent acquisitions

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Noumed’s Australian CDMO business is underpinned by exclusive supply agreements with pharmacy chains — a rare, sticky revenue model in generics; the AUD 20M government grant for Adelaide facility is non-dilutive capital, reducing financial risk; SP Analytics’ 67-dossier pipeline is targeted at patent cliffs within 3 years, creating a high-probability launch runway

commitments.title: Promises (RHP)
commitments.body:
- **Capacity expansion and upgradation of manufacturing facilities (Units I-IV) toward EU-GMP/PIC/S**
- **Establishment of a new R&D centre**
- **Repayment/prepayment of certain outstanding borrowings**
- **Repay bridge/term loan for Noumed acquisition via Sai Parenterals Pte**
- **Complete Noumed Australian factory**

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Expand and upgrade manufacturing capacity (EU-GMP for Units I, II, IV)
- Establish a new R&D centre
- Grow CDMO and export business in Regulated/Semi-Regulated markets
- Integrate Noumed to enter Australia/NZ OTC and government-tender (Pharmac) markets

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Group structure] Subsidiaries: Revat Laboratories (100%, domestic branded generics), SP Analytics (75%, group R&D), Sai Parenterals Pte Limited Singapore (100%, holding company for cross-border transactions), Noumed Pharmaceuticals Pty Limited Australia (74.64%) and Noumed Pharmaceuticals Limited New Zealand (100%). Saicriti Pharma and Prathyak Laboratories would be added at 60% each.
- [US entry] The Board approved incorporation of a US subsidiary to support the Company's preliminary evaluation of entering the US market.
- [Listing] Completed IPO in March 2026 with a primary fund raise of Rs. 285 crore; listed on 2 April 2026 on BSE and NSE.
- [FY27 guidance] The Company reiterates FY27 guidance of Rs. 750 crore revenue at an EBITDA margin of around 17%, with growth weighted towards H2; the deck frames FY27 as "Build", FY28 as "Monetise" and FY29-30 as "Scale".
- [Future project] Land allotted by the Telangana Government for an oncology biosimilars and mAb facility with a technology partner; groundwork begins after the current capex (FY27-28 onwards).
